newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuers contemplate tapping market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuers contemplate tapping market.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond issuers are expected to take advantage of a drop in U.S. Treasury yields, spurred by Friday's market rally, to finance debt, syndicate sources said.
"There's a calendar building but I think the market's kind of suffering from a lack of committment," said one syndicate source.
"After Friday's (employment) numbers, players were left a little confused by the (Treasury) market's rally," he said.
Friday's stronger-than-expected reading on the U.S. labor sector sent the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond down a full point, but it erased its losses minutes later and ended the day higher.

Increased speculation among market players that the Federal Reserve Board will hike interest rates, following a string of stronger-than-expected reports on the U.S. economy, may push issuers to finance debt now, rather than risk higher rates later, dealers said.
"The market shouldn't be where it's at after the (jobs) report so to speak so the issuing environment has improved," said another syndicate source.
"Now the real question is what the Fed will do at its next meeting," said another syndicate source.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the policy setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, is scheduled to meet on September 24 to address U.S. monetary policy.
Meanwhile, a number of deals are lined up to come to market near-term, dealers said.
GTE Hawaiian Telephone Co, a unit of GTE Corp, is expected to price $150 million in 10-year debentures via competitive bid as early as Monday, sources said.
Signet Bank is expected to price $150 million in Baa1/BBB-minus rated 10-year subordinated notes via JP Morgan Securities one day this week.
Among other banks expected to tap the primary market this week are Wells Fargo, Nationsbank, and Key Bank, dealers added.
In the private placement sector, one day this week United USN Inc is expected to set $155 million in eight-year 144A senior notes.
In addition, First Nationwide Holdings is expected to price $525 million in seven-year senior subordinated 144A notes via Smith Barney.
Turning to yankee offerings, Australia & New Zealand Banking Group is expected to price up to $500 million in 10-year yankee subordinated debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Also, European Investment Bank is expected to price between $1.0 to $1.5 billion in 10-year global bonds via joint managers CS First Boston and Lehman Brothers.
In addtiion, Argentaria Bank is also expected to tap the market with a $250 million yankee offering, sources said.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond is up 1/32 at 95-19/32 to yield 7.11 percent, compared with Friday's close at 7.10 percent.
